title: Wavefront Batcher Inspector — continuous workload profiling & safe parameter apply
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We want to reduce per-token unit costs without regressing tail latency or quality. Current autotune components generate static batch profiles that are brittle across multi-tenant workload shifts and microburst patterns. Goal: Build a lightweight continuous profiling + heuristic engine (Wavefront Batcher Inspector) that synthesizes short-term workload signatures, recommends conservative batching parameters, validates them in shadow, and applies changes via a gated progressive roll-forward with automatic rollback on safety triggers. Scope: - Ingest sampled request metadata (seq_len, tokens, model, route, KV-hit-rate, arrival_interarrival distribution) at low overhead. - Create periodic workload fingerprints (1m/5m/1h windows) and classify behavior into a small taxonomy (steady, microburst, prefix-heavy, KV-hot). - Run a rules-first heuristic scorer to propose batch_size, max_latency_slo_ms, prefetch_kv_window, and kv_cache_ttl per model-route cohort. - Validate recommendations in shadow with traffic mirroring and cost/latency delta estimation. - Apply configuration via a staged rollout (shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with guardrails and automatic rollback. Non-goals: - Replacing model-specific kernel/quantization tuning. - Making per-request dynamic batch decisions at inference time (this is a config recommendation system, not the runtime scheduler).
acceptance_criteria: Profiler agent runs on serving nodes and publishes summarized windowed fingerprints with <0.3% p99 CPU overhead
Heuristic scorer outputs a recommended batch profile for a given model-route cohort within 500ms of receiving a fingerprint
Shadow validation produces a cost/latency delta estimate within ±10% of actual when a staged rollout is executed
Staged rollout automation respects SLO gates: p99 latency increase <= 5ms AND error rate delta <= 0.05% OR automatically rolls back
All applied changes are auditable and reversible from the Console (change history, who/when, metric diffs)
technical_approach: Collectors: lightweight sampling agent embedded in request ingress that emits compact fingerprint tuples to existing telemetry pipeline (Kafka -> profiling service)
Fingerprinting: compute per-cohort histograms for seq_len, arrival-IPI, kv-hit-rate; maintain short term decay windows (1m/5m) and long-term baselines (1h)
Heuristics engine: rules-first policy with tunable weights (cost-savings vs latency risk). Start with deterministic rules derived from recent profiling experiments to avoid ML model drift
Shadow validator: route mirrored traffic to a shadow runtime configured with candidate batch params; collect sampled latency/cost metrics and delta estimates over a 10-minute window
Safe-apply controller: orchestrates staged rollout with metric gates and tie-break policies (prefer lower batch sizes on borderline cases), exposes rollback webhooks
Observability: surface per-cohort recommendation rationale, expected cost delta, and live telemetry in the Console heatmap and timeline
Telemetric signals used for gating: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, tokens/sec throughput, KV cache hit ratio, model-side OOM or queue spikes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): run recommendations in mirror mode for 24 hours to gather delta estimates across cohorts
Phase 1 (pilot): apply to <1% traffic for cohorts with clear cost win and margin under SLO gates for 6 hours
Phase 2 (ramped): increase to 5% then 25% with automated checks at each step (2h per step)
Phase 3 (wide): full apply if no gate violations in ramp window; otherwise trigger rollback and create incident review
Emergency rollback: immediate removal of candidate config if metrics exceed critical thresholds (p99 latency +20ms OR error rate +0.5%)
monitoring_and_rollback: Gate evaluation runs every 60s during rollouts. If any gate fails consecutively for 3 windows, rollback is triggered
All rollouts emit a structured event to audit log and create a console snapshot link for the affected cohort
Fallback strategy: if a cohort has no safe candidate, system will mark it as 'no-change' and schedule a follow-up investigation
Post-rollback: auto-attach the last 1h of traces + aggregated request samples to the rollback incident for triage
open_questions: Sampling rate tradeoff: what is the minimal sample rate that yields stable fingerprints across low-volume cohorts? (proposal: 0.5% of requests, configurable)
Cohort definition: should we group by (model, route, customer_tier) or also include input_token_bucket? Need experiments
Heuristic tunables: what initial weightings on cost vs latency risk should be default for Hosted vs Dedicated customers?
Operational cost: storage and retention policy for fingerprints (retain 24h raw, 90d aggregated?)
